Brand Vision (v3.0): "Transforming Global Performance" — TransPerfect's web identity brings transformation to life by expressing how clarity, collaboration and human intelligence drive continual progress. Every asset contributes to a living system that adapts, evolves and connects across every touchpoint.

TransPerfect has 11 official Corporate Core Values: Integrity, Quality, Respect, Service, Diversity, Own It, Teamwork, Transparency, Results, Financial Responsibility, and Urgency. These are the canonical values list and supersede any earlier four-principle visual framing.

Brand Signature: the logo has two core elements — the wordmark and the symbol — and they are treated independently in digital environments. They appear separately depending on context, format and functional needs, with the only exception being the website footer where the full signature may be used.

Wordmark usage: primarily single-color in either white (on dark backgrounds/images) or black (on bright backgrounds/images) across digital channels to ensure consistent sender recognition regardless of background.
Logo safe zone: clear space around the wordmark must be at least 1.5H, where H is the height of the letter T in the wordmark. No other elements may enter this zone.

Logo do-not list: never use off-brand colors, resize/reorder elements, rotate, skew or distort, add effects (e.g. blur), flip, reproduce as a keyline/outline, change typeface, or place over complex backgrounds.

Division sub-brand lockups must scale the industry/sub-brand label in direct proportion to the height (H) of the TransPerfect wordmark to maintain hierarchy. Industry names must always feel connected to — not competing with — the master brand.
Acquired-company endorsement format: "APOSTROPH — A TRANSPERFECT COMPANY". This endorsement lockup pattern signals the parent relationship across the TransPerfect family of sub-brands.

Primary color system anchors on TransPerfect Digital Blue (#003FC7) with deep Dark Blue (#03002C). The system also defines a Dark Blue Gradient and a full web color scheme with accent colors (Lavender, Turquoise, Yellow, Orange) and neutral surfaces (e.g. #e0e8f5 light blue surface).

Typography system: primary typeface plus web-friendly fallback. Headings, body text, and primary/secondary combos are explicitly defined, with multi-weight thickness used for design hierarchy. Headline example demonstrated: "Global content for every mind".

Iconography style is defined as a coherent system applied across industries (Legal, Life Sciences, Media, Games, Government, etc.). Icons follow a single, consistent visual style that supports the master brand and sub-brand hierarchy.

Photography direction: hyper-realistic, human-focused color photography is the primary mode. An additional "Soft Transition" treatment is the approved secondary treatment for blending imagery with brand visuals.

Brand Visuals system has a foundational form with multiple expression states and treatments ("Expression Flex" and "Flexible Expression"). This adaptive visual system is what makes transformation visible through interaction, light and rhythm.
Motion style is part of the master brand system — animations and transitions should embody the brand's sense of continual transformation, clarity and rhythm rather than functioning as decoration.
